title: A Garden for the Harbor
premise: Juniper Underhill built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days after her own engagement collapsed, and she has sworn off believing in them. When her late grandmother's will leaves half of a derelict harbor orchard to Juniper — and the other half to Eli Marchetti, the boy who left town twelve years ago and the man whose family her grandmother blamed for everything — the two are legally bound to restore the orchard together within one year or lose it to a developer. As grafting season becomes harvest, Juniper and Eli unearth the truth about why their families split: a sacrifice her grandmother made to survive that cost Eli's father his name. Juniper must choose between selling her half for the money that would save her failing business and risking the whole heart on a man, an orchard, and a town she stopped letting herself want; they end by keeping the orchard, opening it as a public garden where the town's weddings finally come home.
about_author: C. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former event planner who spent a decade making other people's love stories look effortless before turning to writing them instead. They live in a coastal town much like Harborlight, where they keep a stubborn apple tree of their own and insist it blooms out of spite.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Mail
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Mid-wedding-cake-collapse, she receives a lawyer's letter: her grandmother has died and left her half of Bellwether Orchard. The emotional beat is numb grief interrupted by dread — the orchard is the one place she swore never to return.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Tide
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli gets the same letter in his Boston architecture office and recognizes his own name beside Juniper Underhill's. He hasn't been back since the night his father was driven out of Harborlight. Beat: old anger resurfacing as obligation.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the reading of the will, the lawyer explains the clause: co-restore the orchard within a year, together, or developer Aldous Vane buys it outright. Juniper learns Eli is her co-inheritor and walks out into the rain. Beat: cornered fury.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli arrives at the overgrown orchard and finds Juniper already there with a chainsaw and a grudge. Their first argument ends with both refusing to sell. Beat: sparks that neither will call chemistry.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ruin
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Surveying the property, they find the trees alive under the brambles — including the twin saplings their grandparents planted side by side. A moment of shared wonder interrupts the hostility. Beat: reluctant awe.

chapters.title: Vane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Developer Aldous Vane appears with a generous buyout and a threat wrapped in courtesy. Juniper refuses before Eli can answer, committing them both without asking. Beat: resentment braided with respect.

chapters.title: What Juniper Doesn't Plan Anymore
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Flashback to her broken engagement and the wedding she fled from planning. Back home, her business is bleeding clients. She realizes the orchard restoration could be photographed as a portfolio piece. Beat: pragmatic hope.

chapters.title: Grafting Lessons
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Old-timer Rosa Ferreira teaches them to graft scions; Eli's hands remember more than he expects. Juniper watches him work and hates how easily the years fall away. Beat: tenderness disguised as instruction.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Repairing the farmhouse wall, Juniper finds her grandmother's hidden ledger — payments made secretly to the Marchetti family for years, then abruptly stopped. Beat: the first crack in the official family story.

chapters.title: A Wedding Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. A couple asks to marry in the restored orchard; Juniper, against instinct, takes the booking. Eli sees her transform when she plans, and understands this is how she loves things — at arm's length. Beat: seeing her clearly.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A nor'easter flattens the young grafts. Working through the night to stake them, soaked and laughing, they cross a line neither names. Beat: intimacy born of emergency.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The almost-kiss in the barn, interrupted by Rosa's truck headlights. Eli retreats into blueprints for the garden layout. Beat: fear dressed up as professionalism.

chapters.title: My Mother's Version
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper visits her mother, who repeats the family line: the Marchettis betrayed them, took the money, left. But the mother's certainty sounds rehearsed. Beat: doubt taking root.

chapters.title: His Father's Silence
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli calls his father in Arizona and gets a wall of silence about Harborlight — but hears something underneath it that sounds like guilt. Beat: suspicion turned inward.

chapters.title: First Blossom
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Spring arrives and the orchard blooms all at once. The booked couple visits; Juniper plans their ceremony among the blossoms and feels something dangerous stir. Eli catches her smiling. Beat: guarded joy.

chapters.title: The Business Folds Inward
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Her city business loses its biggest client; Vane's offer starts looking like salvation. She hides the collapse from Eli. Beat: shame and temptation.

chapters.title: Blueprints and Boundaries
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli designs the public garden plan — her grandmother's dream, he realizes, not just the will's demand. He shows Juniper, and for one evening they build a future on paper. Beat: shared vision.

chapters.title: Rosa Tells Half a Story
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Rosa admits the feud began the winter the sardine plant burned — and that Juniper's grandmother testified against Eli's father. But Rosa stops short of why. Beat: history sharpening.

chapters.title: The Fire That Started It
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli digs into archives: his father was accused of setting the fire that destroyed the Underhills' livelihood, and left rather than face trial. The ledger's payments look like hush money — or restitution. Beat: vertigo of inherited blame.

chapters.title: Midsummer Fair
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The town fair; Juniper and Eli run an orchard booth together and the town begins to see them as a pair. Vane watches, recalculating. Beat: belonging, briefly uncomplicated.

chapters.title: Kiss in the Packing Shed
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. After the fair, in the packing shed smelling of apples and dust, they finally kiss. Neither pulls away. Beat: surrender — and the terror that follows it.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper keeps parts of herself back — the failing business, the real reason she fears weddings. Eli senses the withholding and says nothing. Beat: love with a leak in it.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper deciphers the ledger's final entry: the payments stopped the week Eli's father left, and a note reads 'He took the blame so I could keep the land.' Beat: the ground shifting under everything.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli confronts his father by phone: the fire was accidental, caused by the Underhill matriarch's kerosene heater — and she let him take the blame because a Marchetti conviction meant the Underhills kept the waterfront claim. Beat: betrayal reframed across two families.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finds her grandmother's unsent letter of confession, written in her last months: she chose her children's survival over a stranger's name and never forgave herself. Beat: grief complicated by understanding.

chapters.title: The Fight
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli, raw with the truth, accuses Juniper of inheriting the lie along with the land. Juniper, stung, throws his leaving at him — twelve years ago he abandoned her too, the summer before the fire. Beat: both wounds opened at once.

chapters.title: Vane's Deadline
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Vane reveals the will's fine print: if either heir files to sell, the whole orchard goes to him. Juniper's business creditors circle. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli works the orchard alone, deciding whether to sign Vane's papers and be free of Harborlight forever. The twin saplings — one grafted by each grandparent — have grown into each other. Beat: decision ripening.

chapters.title: The Wedding Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper runs the booked couple's rehearsal alone, flawlessly, and realizes mid-ceremony-run that she planned every detail around the life she's pretending not to want. Beat: the mask cracking in public.

chapters.title: Juniper Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper tells Vane no — then drives through the night to Arizona to find Eli's father. Beat: choosing courage over safety.

chapters.title: The Father's Testimony
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. In Arizona, Eli's father gives him a box: the true fire marshal's report, suppressed, proving the accident — kept all these years out of bitterness. 'Go home,' he says. 'Finish what she couldn't.' Beat: inheritance exchanged for release.

chapters.title: The Storm Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper returns to find a hurricane bearing down and Eli already boarding windows. No time for apologies — only work, shoulder to shoulder. Beat: reconciliation through action before words.

chapters.title: Held Against the Wind
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. At the storm's height they shelter in the root cellar, and Juniper finally tells him everything — the broken engagement, the folded business, the fear that she ruins what she touches. Eli stays. Beat: the whole heart, finally risked.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Apples
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The storm spares most of the crop. The town turns out to help harvest — even people who took sides in the old feud. Beat: a community remembering itself.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Play
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Vane, denied the sale, challenges the will's validity in court, claiming the restoration terms were never met. The hearing falls on the eve of the orchard wedding. Beat: climax approaching.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In probate court, Rosa testifies, the suppressed fire report enters evidence, and Juniper speaks for her grandmother — confessing the truth publicly and asking the court to honor the orchard's purpose, not its price. Beat: truth as the only winning move.

chapters.title: Verdict and Vows
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. The judge upholds the will; the deed stands in both names. That evening, the booked couple marries beneath the twin trees, and Juniper plans it with her whole self for the first time. Beat: full-circle joy.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. One year on: the public garden opens, the ledger and confession letter framed in the farmhouse, the town's feuds composted into soil. Juniper signs the guest book of the first community festival. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli proposes in the packing shed, badly, with a ring hidden in a grafting knife roll. Juniper laughs until she cries and says yes before he finishes. Beat: earned sweetness without irony.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The epilogue: spring again, the two of them planting new rows alongside the old trees, teaching town kids to graft. The last image is the twin saplings in full bloom, their branches grown inseparable. Beat: continuation — love as something tended, not found.
